A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 16-page OmniGuard paper, including supplementary Sections A–C. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original localization, watermark fidelity and copyright-recovery experiments in Section 4, plus ablations and supplementary robustness/generalization results in Appendices A and C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including Tables 2–7 and the supplementary qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical dual watermarking procedure, degradation-aware tamper extractor, adaptive watermark transform, AIGC-editing simulator and training objectives.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged: MIRFlickR, DIV2K, COCO and UltraEdit remain, alongside the same editing and degradation scenarios. Appendix C retains MagicQuill, SDXL-inpainting and high-resolution image evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout. Table 2 retains the same five passive localization methods and EditGuard; Table 3 retains PIMoG, SepMark, TrustMark, EditGuard and Robust-Wide. Supplementary comparisons also match.

E3.justification: Both versions document identical sample counts, image resolutions, metrics, training settings and attack procedures. This includes the 1,000-image COCO and UltraEdit evaluations and the supplementary experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The watermark-selection and extractor ablations in Tables 4–5, joint-training comparison in Table 6, VAE residual analysis, and supplementary robustness, generalization and fidelity analyses are identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged throughout both PDFs. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, OmniGuard's degraded Stable Diffusion Inpaint F1 remains 0.947 in Table 2, and its dual-watermark PSNR remains 41.78 dB in Table 3. Appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including the corruption model, extraction formulation, reversible transforms, simulator and losses, are identical. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain identical claims about hybrid localization, copyright protection, fidelity, flexibility and robustness, including the claimed improvements over EditGuard.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability boundaries are unchanged. Both retain the whole-image localization qualification for global edits and Appendix A.1's limitations concerning severe degradation and watermark artifacts from high-resolution scaling.

D1.justification: Sections 3.6 and 4.1 and Appendix B provide identical hyperparameters, optimizers, hardware and architecture details. No implementation or resource-access information is added, removed or revised.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning relative to prior watermarking and localization methods, and all 68 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 2 December 2024 to v2 dated 1 March 2025. All paper prose, author information, headings and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12, Tables 1–7 and their placement and formatting are unchanged. Pages 2–16 render identically; first-page pixel differences are confined to the version/date stamp text, with no layout change.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves v1's scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, limitations and presentation, including all appendices. Updating the administrative arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully affect the paper's quality.
